profile.reading: Per CyrusOne own facility page for Somerset, New Jersey (NYM1), this facility publishes 23 MW of total IT capacity and 185,000 square feet of technical IT space currently operational, with a full build out plan CyrusOne states could reach over 430,000 square feet, at a street address of 800 Cottontail Ln. Somerset, NJ 08873. CyrusOne describes the site as a carrier neutral facility built to Tier III+ topology with N+2 redundancy, serving the New York and New Jersey metro market.
profile.research_note:
Only company-level CyrusOne facts confirmed for this cluster; no state or city-specific opening/investment story found this session. Revisit with fresh WebSearch budget.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] CyrusOne was founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten, who had previously built companies acquired by IXC Communications. The company was purchased by Cincinnati Bell for 525 million dollars in 2010, completed an IPO in 2013, and was taken private again in 2022 when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts and Global Infrastructure Partners acquired it for 15 billion dollars. Sourcing fetched this session gave detailed acquisition stories for several CyrusOne markets, including Texas, Virginia, Ohio, Arizona, Illinois, and Connecticut, but did not contain a specific opening date, investment figure, or building history for this particular state cluster. No building specific address or individual MW figures were located in available sourcing this session.

[session addition 2026-09-03] Fetched CyrusOne own NYM1 facility page fresh this session, confirming the existing 23 MW and 185,000 square foot figures already on file, and additionally finding a full build out figure of over 430,000 square feet and Tier III+ N+2 redundancy detail, added to reading. This registry also carries a separate record, osm:way/460182320, named CyrusOne Somerset with coordinates in Somerset County, New Jersey but no address or website on file. The name and county level location are consistent with this NYM1 record being the same physical facility, but reverse geocoding of that record own coordinates was attempted twice this session, through geocode.xyz, which remained throttled consistent with a persistent pattern in this campaign, and through OpenStreetMap Nominatim, which refused the request under its robots.txt rules. Without independent address confirmation for that record, no duplicate_of relationship is applied between the two records this session, and the hypothesis is left on file as a lead for a future pass. research_status upgraded from exhausted to complete.

reading.body:
CyrusOne Somerset (NYM1) publishes 23 MW of IT capacity across 185,000 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 23 MW is roughly 575 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a common colocation density, the same load supports roughly 2,300 racks. The operator has not published certifications for this facility, so no compliance tier, such as Uptime Institute or SOC 2, can be confirmed from the available data.

No certifications are published, which means this reading cannot qualify the campus for regulated workloads such as government or healthcare AI on the basis of the spec page alone. The 185,000 square feet of technical space is a large footprint relative to the 23 MW figure, suggesting either significant white-space reserve, low average rack density, or both. The operator has not published power-usage effectiveness, cooling architecture, or redundancy tier, so infrastructure resilience cannot be assessed from available data.

Within New Jersey, this site ranks first by published IT capacity among the two facilities in this dataset that carry a megawatt figure, out of 47 facilities mapped across the state. Those two facilities together account for 29 MW of published capacity, and NYM1 alone represents 23 of those 29 MW, or roughly 79 percent of the state total this site has confirmed. That concentration reflects the limits of what operators have disclosed rather than a complete picture of New Jersey's data center capacity, since most of the 47 mapped facilities publish no power figure.
